findings.issue_text: [BUG] Calling prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany with an empty data object throws a Prisma validation error, so getAvailability crashes on every cache-refresh path. Prisma updateMany with `data: {}` fails validation ("Argument data must provide at least one field") or produces an invalid UPDATE with no SET clause; every Google Calendar availability fetch that reaches this line (i.e., every cache-miss fetch for a Google credential) throws, breaking booking availability for Google users.

[BUG] `sed -i '' -E` is macOS-only syntax; on Linux GNU sed the empty suffix is treated as a filename and the script exits with an error instead of updating GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL. Any developer running this script on Linux (or CI) gets `sed: can't read : No such file or directory`, the env file is left stale pointing at the previous tunnel URL, and webhook testing silently targets the wrong host.

[ADVISORY] The ownership check `userId: user.id` returns no credential for delegation-managed calendars (userId is null on those credentials), but the UI in CredentialActionsDropdown shows the delete-cache action whenever cacheUpdatedAt is set regardless of canDisconnect. For a delegation Google credential whose cache rows exist, a user clicks "Yes, delete cache" and receives the generic "Error deleting cache" toast every time because the handler throws "Credential not found or access denied" — a UI action that can never succeed.

[ADVISORY] SelectedCalendarRepository is referenced in getAvailabilityCache but no import for it appears in this diff; if the pre-existing file does not already import it, this is a compile-time failure. If the module lacks an existing import of SelectedCalendarRepository from @calcom/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar, the package fails to build and every consumer of GoogleCalendarService breaks; verify the ambient import exists before merge.

[BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object, so Prisma generates no SET clause and SelectedCalendar.updatedAt is never touched — the stated intent of the call is not achieved. If Prisma rejects empty update data (it errors on empty `data` for updateMany in current versions), every getAvailability call on the Google calendar path throws; if it silently no-ops, the freshness signal this line was added to maintain never updates and the new schema fields selected in getConnectedDestinationCalendars/user.ts are write-dead.

[ADVISORY] The handler hard-imports the concrete CalendarCacheRepository instead of going through the interface/mock selection used everywhere else, so deployments with the calendar-cache feature disabled get the real repository on this new path. The CalendarCacheRepositoryMock exists precisely because disabled deployments must not touch the cache store; this new query bypasses that switch, so a disabled-deployment user opening the calendars settings page now executes a groupBy against CalendarCache that was previously guaranteed never to run (or crashes if the store isn't provisioned).

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheHandler deletes cache rows via raw prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany, bypassing ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential (whose mock is designed to no-op on disabled deployments). On an instance with calendar-cache disabled, clicking the new 'Delete cached data' menu item runs a deleteMany the mock layer was built to skip; the feature-flag behavior of every other cache operation is silently violated on this one path.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation has no onSettled invalidation of viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (unlike disconnectMutation on lines 49-56), so cacheUpdatedAt in the query cache stays populated after a successful delete. After confirming deletion, any rendering of connectedCalendars not driven by the parent's onSuccess refetch (e.g. the AppListCard listing that reads the same query from cache) still shows the stale 'Last updated' status and the destructive delete action, until some unrelated refetch occurs.

[ADVISORY] The not-found/denied path throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError, so the client receives an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR-shaped failure for what is a 4xx authorization condition. A user hitting a stale credentialId (e.g. after disconnecting in another tab) gets the generic 'Error deleting cache' toast backed by a 500-logged server error rather than a proper NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code; error monitoring also logs it as a server fault.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds three behavior-bearing units — deleteCache handler (auth + delete semantics), getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy, and CredentialActionsDropdown render gating — with no test files anywhere in the diff. A regression in the credential-ownership check in deleteCacheHandler would let any authed user delete another user's calendar cache rows (the where clause is the only guard) and nothing in CI would catch it; the groupBy max-updatedAt mapping and the canDisconnect/hasCache null-render gating (which silently removes the disconnect button for delegation creds) are likewise unverified.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' Intl.DateTimeFormat, ignoring the user's locale that the component already has via useLocale. Non-English users see US-formatted dates in an otherwise localized settings page.

[ADVISORY] A developer-local Tunnelmole webhook testing script is shipped in a PR whose stated intent is calendar cache status and actions. Repo maintainers inherit a 79-line dev-tooling script (with a hardcoded relative ../.env path and macOS-only `sed -i ''`) that has no CI hook, no docs, and no requirement in this feature; anyone auditing the diff cannot trace it to intent.

[ADVISORY] The dev:cron runner is switched from ts-node to npx tsx, unrelated to calendar cache status. An untraceable toolchain change bundled into a feature PR; if tsx is not a declared dependency in apps/web, every dev running `yarn dev:cron` incurs an npx download or resolution failure, and the change ships unreviewed alongside the cache feature.

[BUG] The added SelectedCalendar.updatedAt 'update' passes an empty data object `{}`, making updateManyByCredentialId a no-op that touches every matching row without changing anything. The stated intent (surfacing cache freshness via SelectedCalendar.updatedAt) is not implemented: the write sets no fields, so updatedAt never reflects cache refreshes; meanwhile the code (and the widened SelectedCalendar selects for updatedAt/googleChannelId in user.ts and getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts) adds dead surface — no consumer reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for cache status anywhere in the diff, which uses CalendarCache.updatedAt instead. This block is implementation work traceable to no enforced invariant.

[ADVISORY] The mechanical removal of the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` type assertion in findMany is an unrelated refactor inside this feature PR. Behavior-neutral churn that loses type-checking of args against the Prisma type; reviewers of a cache-status feature must audit unrelated persistence-layer changes, and future callers lose the compile-time arg validation the satisfies clause provided.

[ADVISORY] The UserWithCalendars type is widened to include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on allSelectedCalendars/userLevelSelectedCalendars, but no code in this diff reads those fields through this type. Speculative type-surface expansion with no consumer; the next reader assumes cache status flows through SelectedCalendar (it actually flows through the separate CalendarCache groupBy query), so the widened type misleads rather than documents and is deletion-safe today.

[BUG] The deleteCache feature deletes only CalendarCache rows for the credential but leaves the per-calendar free-busy cache in Redis/whatever backing CachedCalendarMutex-free paths use untouched for delegation-credential calendars, and the PR adds no corresponding cache-invalidation for non-Google or delegated credentials — under-scoped relative to 'delete cached data' action presented in the UI. Users on organization-managed (delegated) Google credentials see no cache dropdown at all (hasCache requires cacheUpdatedAt, and delegated flows populate differently), and users deleting cache for a credential whose entries were written under a different userId key get a partial delete presented as 'Cache deleted successfully' while stale free-busy data continues to be served from the remaining rows.

[BUG] getAvailability calls updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty data payload, which Prisma rejects for updateMany (empty data objects are a validation error), so every Google availability check on the booking path throws. After this change, the availability lookup for Google Calendar-connected users fails at the cache-refresh step, breaking booking page availability — the happy-path cache read now depends on a write that itself crashes; and even where Prisma tolerates it, an empty payload with @updatedAt only bumps the timestamp when other fields are written, so the 'cache freshness' signal is never actually set.

[BUG] The write path and the read path for 'cache status' use two different tables: the touch writes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, but the UI's cacheUpdatedAt comes from CalendarCache groupBy _max updatedAt (connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28-34), so the value the feature writes is never the value the feature displays. The SelectedCalendar.updatedAt touch is dead data for this feature; the displayed 'Last updated' timestamp only advances when a CalendarCache row happens to be (re)written, and the two signals drift independently — a user deletes the cache, the UI shows null, while SelectedCalendars still claim a fresh updatedAt no consumer reads.

[ADVISORY] The SelectedCalendar write runs unconditionally after every getAvailability call, adding a DB write (UPDATE over all rows where credentialId matches) to the hot availability-check path that previously served from cache without any write. Every booking-page availability fetch for Google users now issues an extra multi-row UPDATE; at booking-page traffic volume this multiplies write load and row contention on SelectedCalendar for zero consumer of the written value (see the read-path mismatch), a hot-path regression the cache was supposed to avoid.

[BUG] The access-denied / not-found branch throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError, so an unauthorized or stale credentialId returns an INTERNAL_ERROR (500) rather than a 4xx the tRPC contract implies. A user whose credential was deleted (or passing another user's credentialId) gets a 500 with generic 'Error deleting cache' toast and noise in error monitoring, instead of a clean NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN.

[ADVISORY] The backfill sets updatedAt = NOW() for all legacy CalendarCache rows, so the 'Last updated' the UI now displays is the migration timestamp, not when the cache was actually populated. Immediately after deploy, every Google-connected user sees a bogus 'Last updated' equal to deploy time for cached data that may be days old, misleading the delete-cache decision the UI exists to support.

[ADVISORY] getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns rows only for credentials that have cache rows, and the handler fills misses with null, conflating 'calendar-cache feature disabled' (mock returns []) with 'no cache exists', which the UI then renders as cache-absent. On installs where calendar-cache is disabled (CalendarCacheRepositoryMock), connectedCalendars silently reports no cache for Google credentials, so the delete-cache UI and status line disappear with no signal distinguishing feature-off from empty cache — operators cannot tell misconfiguration from intended behavior.

[ADVISORY] updateManyByCredentialId takes Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, exposing raw Prisma update semantics at the repository boundary for a call site whose only purpose is a timestamp touch, and the schema reuses the generic SelectedCalendar.updatedAt column (shared with @updatedAt on every other mutation) as the cache-freshness channel. Any other SelectedCalendar update (rename, watch-error set, delegation changes) silently bumps the same updatedAt column, so a future consumer reading it as 'cache last refreshed' gets timestamps polluted by unrelated writes; the next change gets riskier because two meanings share one column with no separate cacheCheckedAt field.

[BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object ({}), which Prisma rejects for updateMany, so the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump the comment promises never happens. Every getAvailability cache-miss path that reaches this line throws a Prisma validation error ("data" must not be empty / no update fields), breaking availability lookups for Google Calendar users whenever cache is cold — and even if tolerated, the empty payload means @updatedAt is not bumped, so the cache-status timestamp the whole PR was built to display is never refreshed by this code path.

[ADVISORY] The PR title and server-side changes implement cache status/delete generically (CalendarCache table, deleteCache mutation, repository method are calendar-type-agnostic), but the UI silently narrows the feature to Google Calendar only via hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt. Users of any other cached calendar provider see no cache status or delete action at all, while their CalendarCache rows keep accumulating — the accepted objective ("calendar cache status and actions") was reduced to a Google-only feature during iteration without an explicit scope decision being recorded; whoever accepted the PR accepted a different surface than what was implemented.

[ADVISORY] Two parallel mechanisms track "cache last updated" — the new CalendarCache.updatedAt max via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds and the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump added in CalendarService.ts — with no single source of truth. The displayed timestamp (CalendarCache._max.updatedAt) and the value GoogleCalendarService writes to refresh cache staleness signals (SelectedCalendar.updatedAt) are different rows updated on different schedules, so the status shown to users will diverge from the mechanism intended to validate it; the next change to cache semantics requires updating both sites or the UI lies. Also note getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns no row for credentials with zero cached entries, which the map lookup silently coerces to null — an empty cache is indistinguishable from "no status".

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess does not invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation's onSettled which does. After a user deletes cached data, the dropdown's "Last updated" line continues showing the pre-deletion timestamp if the parent's onSuccess/onChanged doesn't refetch this exact query, presenting a cache status for data that no longer exists.

[ADVISORY] A developer-local Tunnelmole test harness with hardcoded paths (/tmp/tmole.log, ../.env, sed -i '' which is macOS-only) is shipped in the production scripts directory as part of a user-facing cache-status feature PR. Linux contributors running the script get a sed syntax error at the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL rewrite (BSD-only -i '' form), and the repo accumulates an unreproducible dev-only script unrelated to the PR's accepted intent.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US") inside a component that already calls useLocale(), so the accepted i18n intent (all user-facing strings localized, as the new common.json entries show) is broken for this value. Non-English users see a fully translated dropdown except for a US-formatted English date/time, and the i18n pipeline cannot fix it because the locale never flows from t().

[ADVISORY] The handler throws a bare Error instead of a TRPCError, so an unauthorized or missing credentialId yields an HTTP 500 with an 'Internal Server Error' rather than a 4xx the tRPC contract implies. Users who pass a credentialId they don't own (or a stale one after disconnect) get a 500 error toast; server logs fill with unhandled errors and clients cannot distinguish auth failure from server fault.

[BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object `{}`, so it never updates SelectedCalendar.updatedAt despite the comment claiming it does — Prisma updateMany with empty `data` performs no column update (and the new `updatedAt` bump the feature depends on is never written), so the 'Last updated' cache status shown in the dropdown goes stale forever on the webhook/refresh path. After a cache refresh via getAvailability, the CalendarCache rows get new updatedAt values but the SelectedCalendar rows do not (if any consumer reads them), and if Prisma rejects empty data the availability call itself errors; the cache-status UI never reflects the refresh this code was added to record.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` even though the component already calls useLocale(), so every non-English user sees an en-US formatted date in an otherwise localized string. Non-English users of the calendar settings page get a jarring English-locale date inside the localized 'cache_last_updated' text; fix is to pass the locale from useLocale() (or use the platform's date formatting util).

[ADVISORY] The mock's getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns `[]` (sentinel for 'no cache info') which the handler then maps to `cacheUpdatedAt: null`, making the cache-status UI silently disappear in any environment where calendar-cache is disabled — indistinguishable from a user who genuinely has no cached data. Developers/instances running with the calendar-cache feature disabled cannot exercise or verify the cache-status UI path at all, and any future test relying on the mock verifies the hide-behavior of a sentinel rather than real cache-status semantics.

[BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object, which Prisma rejects with a PrismaClientValidationError before any rows are updated. prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: ..., data: {} }) throws "Value argument `data` must not be empty" on every call, so getAvailability/cached-availability-check now throws a 500 on every request for Google credentials instead of bumping updatedAt — the intended updatedAt refresh never happens and the availability endpoint breaks for all Google-connected users.

[ADVISORY] getCacheStatusByCredentialIds computes the max updatedAt over all rows including expired cache rows, with no filter on expiresAt. Because expired rows are only cleaned lazily (or never, since deleteManyByCredential is a manual action), the Cache Status shown in the dropdown reports a "last updated" timestamp for a credential whose cached entries are all expired, so users see a status that misrepresents the actual cache state.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess calls onSuccess?.() but never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation which invalidates queries in onSettled. If a caller passes no onSuccess (or the caller's refetch is conditional), the connected-calendars cache retains the pre-delete cacheUpdatedAt, so the dropdown keeps offering 'Delete cached data' and showing a stale timestamp until an unrelated refetch occurs.

[ADVISORY] deleteCache deletes CalendarCache rows but leaves SelectedCalendar.updatedAt untouched, while the code elsewhere treats SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as the sync marker refreshed on cache write. After a user deletes the cache, the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt marker still reflects the last write; any consumer keying off that marker (e.g. webhook-driven invalidation or cache freshness logic) sees a fresh timestamp while the actual cache rows are gone, producing inconsistent state until the next availability fetch backfills it.

[BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object `{}`, which Prisma rejects with a validation error, so the cache-miss refresh path in getAvailabilityFromCache throws instead of completing. Every cache-miss availability lookup (booking page load, free-busy check) for Google Calendar credentials fails after the fetch and setAvailabilityInCache succeed — the user gets a 500/error instead of availability, and the freshly written cache is never reached as a successful response. Prisma updateMany requires a non-empty `data`; `data: {}` throws `PrismaClientValidationError` at runtime.

[BUG] The handler throws a plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a `TRPCError` with a BAD_REQUEST/FORBIDDEN code, so the client receives an internal-error-shaped 500 rather than the 4xx-shaped error the tRPC mutation contract elsewhere provides. A user clicking delete on a stale credential entry (credential already removed elsewhere) gets an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR-shaped response and the generic 'error_deleting_cache' toast meant for unexpected failures, instead of a proper not-found/bad-request shape; monitoring also records it as a server error rather than client error.

[ADVISORY] deleteCache bypasses CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential and calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly, creating a second deletion path that diverges from the repository abstraction (the mock logs and skips, this one does not). Any future behavior added to the repository's deleteManyByCredential (event channel invalidation, cache-bust keys, logging) silently won't apply to the user-facing delete action; operators on calendar-cache-disabled deployments get cache rows deleted here that the mock path would have preserved.

[ADVISORY] The handler unconditionally constructs the real CalendarCacheRepository and queries the CalendarCache table even when the calendar-cache feature is disabled (where the rest of the codebase substitutes the Mock repository), so the connected-calendars query always incurs a groupBy on CalendarCache. Every settings-page connected-calendars fetch pays an extra unindexed groupBy on calendarCache (groupBy on credentialId with no composite index covering it beyond the unique key prefix) even on deployments where the cache is disabled, and those rows can be stale legacy data from before the feature flag existed, showing a bogus 'Last updated' to users.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation has no onSettled invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike disconnectMutation), so after a successful delete the list still shows the old cache timestamp until onSuccess's parent refetch, and after failure nothing refreshes. When callers pass no `onSuccess` (the prop is optional), a successful cache delete leaves the 'Last updated' row stale in the open dropdown until a manual reload, and any error leaves stale UI with no state reconciliation; only the toast tells the user anything happened.

[ADVISORY] `sed -i '' -E` uses the macOS-only empty-suffix form; on GNU/Linux sed this fails with "extra characters at the end of h command", so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated on Linux. Any developer on Linux running the script hits a sed error after the tunnel is already up and the .env write is skipped, leaving a stale webhook URL that makes the subsequent webhook test silently target the old host.

This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in `CalendarService.ts`. That method directly calls `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`, so it will execute `updateMany` with `data: {}`. Prisma’s `updateMany` expects at least one field in `data`; passing an empty object is a likely runtime validation error (or invalid SQL with no SET), which would make the availability refresh path throw at runtime.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, the delete-cache action is shown whenever `hasCache` is true (`const hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt;`), even when `canDisconnect` is false due to `delegationCredentialId` being set. However, the `deleteCacheHandler` authorizes strictly by `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id } })` and throws if not found. The diff explicitly treats delegation credentials specially (comments: “Delegation credential can't be disconnected”), so it’s plausible these credentials won’t satisfy `userId: user.id`, making the UI-presented delete-cache action non-functional for such entries and always resulting in the generic error toast (`onError` -> `t("error_deleting_cache")`).

If the module lacks an existing import of SelectedCalendarRepository from @calcom/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar, the package fails to build and every consumer of GoogleCalendarService breaks; verify the ambient import exists before merge.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new usage of `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(...)` in `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, but the shown hunk does not include any corresponding import changes. Whether this is a compile-time bug depends on whether `SelectedCalendarRepository` was already imported earlier in the file (not shown in the diff), so it’s a concrete check to perform but not a verifiable defect from the diff alone.

If Prisma rejects empty update data (it errors on empty `data` for updateMany in current versions), every getAvailability call on the Google calendar path throws; if it silently no-ops, the freshness signal this line was added to maintain never updates and the new schema fields selected in getConnectedDestinationCalendars/user.ts are write-dead.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the new code directly imports and instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` (`new CalendarCacheRepository()`) and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)`. The diff also shows there is an `ICalendarCacheRepository` interface and a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` explicitly meant to be used when calendar-cache is disabled (it logs "Skipping ... due to calendar-cache being disabled"). This new path bypasses any existing indirection/feature-flag-based repository selection mechanism, creating an architectural/configuration inconsistency. Whether it actually crashes in disabled deployments is not provable from the diff alone, but the hard-wiring is verifiable and actionable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteCacheHandler` directly calling `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` in `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, while the calendar-cache abstraction exists (`ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential` and a mock that explicitly no-ops “due to calendar-cache being disabled”). This is a concrete, diff-grounded architectural inconsistency/bypass of the repository layer. However, the claim that this *definitely* violates a feature-flag/disabled-deployment behavior cannot be verified from the diff alone (no wiring is shown proving the mock is used in those deployments), so it’s better classified as an important design issue rather than a proven defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation has no onSettled invalidation of viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars (unlike disconnectMutation on lines 49-56), so cacheUpdatedAt in the query cache stays populated after a successful delete. After confirming deletion, any rendering of connectedCalendars not driven by the parent's onSuccess refetch (e.g. the AppListCard listing that reads the same query from cache) still shows the stale 'Last updated' status and the destructive delete action, until some unrelated refetch occurs.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess?.()` but does not invalidate or refetch any TRPC queries. In contrast, `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `utils.viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`. Since `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` now enriches each connected calendar with `cacheUpdatedAt` from the DB, deleting cache via `deleteCache.handler.ts` changes server state but will not update the client-side `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` cache unless the parent’s `onSuccess` happens to refetch/invalidate. From the diff alone, the dropdown component itself leaves the query cache potentially stale after deletion.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The not-found/denied path throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError, so the client receives an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR-shaped failure for what is a 4xx authorization condition. A user hitting a stale credentialId (e.g. after disconnecting in another tab) gets the generic 'Error deleting cache' toast backed by a 500-logged server error rather than a proper NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code; error monitoring also logs it as a server fault.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds three behavior-bearing units — deleteCache handler (auth + delete semantics), getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy, and CredentialActionsDropdown render gating — with no test files anywhere in the diff. A regression in the credential-ownership check in deleteCacheHandler would let any authed user delete another user's calendar cache rows (the where clause is the only guard) and nothing in CI would catch it; the groupBy max-updatedAt mapping and the canDisconnect/hasCache null-render gating (which silently removes the disconnect button for delegation creds) are likewise unverified.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new behavior in multiple places without any accompanying test changes: (1) new TRPC mutation `viewer.calendars.deleteCache` and `deleteCacheHandler` that enforces ownership via `prisma.credential.findFirst({ where: { id: credentialId, userId: user.id }})` before `calendarCache.deleteMany` (security-sensitive logic, but untested in this diff); (2) new repository method `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` using `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy` and mapping `_max.updatedAt` into `cacheUpdatedAt` in `connectedCalendarsHandler` (data-shaping logic, untested); and (3) new `CredentialActionsDropdown` render gating (`if (!canDisconnect && !hasCache) return null;`) which changes when the actions UI is present and what it contains (behavioral UI logic, untested). The finding’s “any authed user could delete another user’s cache” is hypothetical (the current guard exists in the diff), but the core review issue—new nontrivial/security-relevant logic added with no tests in the diff—is specific and diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded 'en-US' Intl.DateTimeFormat, ignoring the user's locale that the component already has via useLocale. Non-English users see US-formatted dates in an otherwise localized settings page.

[ADVISORY] A developer-local Tunnelmole webhook testing script is shipped in a PR whose stated intent is calendar cache status and actions. Repo maintainers inherit a 79-line dev-tooling script (with a hardcoded relative ../.env path and macOS-only `sed -i ''`) that has no CI hook, no docs, and no requirement in this feature; anyone auditing the diff cannot trace it to intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly adds a new developer-local script `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` (79 lines) that starts `tmole`, parses its log, and rewrites `../.env` using a macOS-specific `sed -i ''` invocation. This is unrelated to the primary cache-status/action changes elsewhere in the PR and introduces repo maintenance/scope concerns (undocumented dev tool, OS-specific behavior, hardcoded relative env path) rather than a direct runtime defect in the feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The dev:cron runner is switched from ts-node to npx tsx, unrelated to calendar cache status. An untraceable toolchain change bundled into a feature PR; if tsx is not a declared dependency in apps/web, every dev running `yarn dev:cron` incurs an npx download or resolution failure, and the change ships unreviewed alongside the cache feature.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `apps/web/package.json` script `dev:cron` from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, which is a tooling/workflow change unrelated to the calendar cache feature changes shown elsewhere. The diff does not show `tsx` being added as a local dependency, so reviewers cannot confirm from this PR alone that `yarn dev:cron` will be reproducible without relying on `npx` resolution behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The added SelectedCalendar.updatedAt 'update' passes an empty data object `{}`, making updateManyByCredentialId a no-op that touches every matching row without changing anything. The stated intent (surfacing cache freshness via SelectedCalendar.updatedAt) is not implemented: the write sets no fields, so updatedAt never reflects cache refreshes; meanwhile the code (and the widened SelectedCalendar selects for updatedAt/googleChannelId in user.ts and getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts) adds dead surface — no consumer reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt for cache status anywhere in the diff, which uses CalendarCache.updatedAt instead. This block is implementation work traceable to no enforced invariant.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService.updateAvailabilityInCache`, the new call `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` passes an empty `data` object to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany` (see `updateManyByCredentialId`). With no fields set, this cannot reliably achieve the stated intent of “Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt” and is likely either a no-op (leaving `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` unchanged) or a runtime/validation error depending on Prisma behavior. Additionally, the diff’s cache freshness UI/logic is driven by `CalendarCache.updatedAt` (`CalendarCache` schema + `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` + `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` enrichment) and does not read `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, making this write both incorrect for its comment and unused by the implemented feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The mechanical removal of the `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` type assertion in findMany is an unrelated refactor inside this feature PR. Behavior-neutral churn that loses type-checking of args against the Prisma type; reviewers of a cache-status feature must audit unrelated persistence-layer changes, and future callers lose the compile-time arg validation the satisfies clause provided.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `SelectedCalendarRepository.findMany` from building `args` with `satisfies Prisma.SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs` to directly passing `{ where, select, orderBy }` into `prisma.selectedCalendar.findMany`. This is behavior-neutral but removes the compile-time validation that the constructed args conform to Prisma’s `SelectedCalendarFindManyArgs`, and it’s an unrelated persistence-layer refactor within a cache-status feature PR that adds review churn.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The UserWithCalendars type is widened to include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on allSelectedCalendars/userLevelSelectedCalendars, but no code in this diff reads those fields through this type. Speculative type-surface expansion with no consumer; the next reader assumes cache status flows through SelectedCalendar (it actually flows through the separate CalendarCache groupBy query), so the widened type misleads rather than documents and is deletion-safe today.

adjudication.rationale: The diff widens `UserWithCalendars` to include `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` on `allSelectedCalendars`/`userLevelSelectedCalendars` (packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts) and updates the `UserRepository` select to fetch those fields (packages/lib/server/repository/user.ts). However, the cache UI/data flow added in this PR is sourced via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` and injected as `cacheUpdatedAt` in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, not via `SelectedCalendar` fields. Nothing in this diff consumes `updatedAt`/`googleChannelId` via the widened `UserWithCalendars` surface, so the expansion appears unnecessary and potentially confusing, though not a correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The deleteCache feature deletes only CalendarCache rows for the credential but leaves the per-calendar free-busy cache in Redis/whatever backing CachedCalendarMutex-free paths use untouched for delegation-credential calendars, and the PR adds no corresponding cache-invalidation for non-Google or delegated credentials — under-scoped relative to 'delete cached data' action presented in the UI. Users on organization-managed (delegated) Google credentials see no cache dropdown at all (hasCache requires cacheUpdatedAt, and delegated flows populate differently), and users deleting cache for a credential whose entries were written under a different userId key get a partial delete presented as 'Cache deleted successfully' while stale free-busy data continues to be served from the remaining rows.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteCache` only deleting rows from the `CalendarCache` table via Prisma (`prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })`) and the UI strings/actions are clearly scoped to this “cache” (new `CalendarCache.updatedAt`, `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, and `cacheUpdatedAt` in connected calendars). Claims about Redis/“CachedCalendarMutex-free paths”, non-Google caches, and delegated-calendar flows being populated differently are not evidenced anywhere in the diff. Also, the finding’s assertion that rows written under a different `userId` would remain is contradicted by the deletion predicate: it deletes by `credentialId` only, regardless of `userId`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] getAvailability calls updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with an empty data payload, which Prisma rejects for updateMany (empty data objects are a validation error), so every Google availability check on the booking path throws. After this change, the availability lookup for Google Calendar-connected users fails at the cache-refresh step, breaking booking page availability — the happy-path cache read now depends on a write that itself crashes; and even where Prisma tolerates it, an empty payload with @updatedAt only bumps the timestamp when other fields are written, so the 'cache freshness' signal is never actually set.

adjudication.rationale: In `GoogleCalendarService` a new call was added: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` (empty `data`). The repository method is implemented as `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`, so this will call Prisma with `data: {}`. An empty update payload is not a meaningful update and is very likely to be rejected by Prisma validation at runtime (or, if it were accepted, it would not reliably update `updatedAt` as the comment intends). Either way, the diff shows a newly introduced write on the availability path that does not actually specify any fields to update, which can break availability checks.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The write path and the read path for 'cache status' use two different tables: the touch writes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, but the UI's cacheUpdatedAt comes from CalendarCache groupBy _max updatedAt (connectedCalendars.handler.ts:28-34), so the value the feature writes is never the value the feature displays. The SelectedCalendar.updatedAt touch is dead data for this feature; the displayed 'Last updated' timestamp only advances when a CalendarCache row happens to be (re)written, and the two signals drift independently — a user deletes the cache, the UI shows null, while SelectedCalendars still claim a fresh updatedAt no consumer reads.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the UI’s `cacheUpdatedAt` is populated from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` and the `groupBy` `_max.updatedAt` in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`. Separately, `GoogleCalendarService` adds a call to `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` with a comment about updating `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`, but nothing in this diff uses `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` to drive the displayed cache status. This is a real inconsistency/architecture concern (extra write / misleading signal), but it’s not verifiably a functional defect in the cache-status feature because the displayed timestamp is explicitly defined to come from `CalendarCache`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The SelectedCalendar write runs unconditionally after every getAvailability call, adding a DB write (UPDATE over all rows where credentialId matches) to the hot availability-check path that previously served from cache without any write. Every booking-page availability fetch for Google users now issues an extra multi-row UPDATE; at booking-page traffic volume this multiplies write load and row contention on SelectedCalendar for zero consumer of the written value (see the read-path mismatch), a hot-path regression the cache was supposed to avoid.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, an unconditional call was added after the cache-miss block: `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});`. Because it sits outside `if (!cachedData) { ... }`, it will run even when availability is served from cache, adding an extra `updateMany` DB operation on the hot availability path. The review concern about increased write load/row contention is thus diff-grounded (the “no consumer of the value” part is less directly verifiable from this diff).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The access-denied / not-found branch throws a plain Error instead of a TRPCError, so an unauthorized or stale credentialId returns an INTERNAL_ERROR (500) rather than a 4xx the tRPC contract implies. A user whose credential was deleted (or passing another user's credentialId) gets a 500 with generic 'Error deleting cache' toast and noise in error monitoring, instead of a clean NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN.

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the not-found/unauthorized branch does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when the credential isn’t owned by the user. In tRPC, throwing a plain `Error` typically surfaces as an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR`/500 rather than a 4xx-style `TRPCError` (e.g., `NOT_FOUND`/`FORBIDDEN`), causing the client to get a generic failure and generating avoidable error monitoring noise. This behavior is directly introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The backfill sets updatedAt = NOW() for all legacy CalendarCache rows, so the 'Last updated' the UI now displays is the migration timestamp, not when the cache was actually populated. Immediately after deploy, every Google-connected user sees a bogus 'Last updated' equal to deploy time for cached data that may be days old, misleading the delete-cache decision the UI exists to support.

adjudication.rationale: The migration adds `CalendarCache.updatedAt` as `NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()` (migration.sql) and Prisma schema sets `updatedAt @default(now()) @updatedAt`. For existing rows, this backfills `updatedAt` to the migration/deploy time regardless of when the cached value was originally populated. The UI surfaces this via `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` using `_max.updatedAt` from `calendarCache.groupBy(...)` and displays it as `cache_last_updated` in `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`. So immediately after deploy, legacy cache rows will misleadingly appear “Last updated” at deploy time.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns rows only for credentials that have cache rows, and the handler fills misses with null, conflating 'calendar-cache feature disabled' (mock returns []) with 'no cache exists', which the UI then renders as cache-absent. On installs where calendar-cache is disabled (CalendarCacheRepositoryMock), connectedCalendars silently reports no cache for Google credentials, so the delete-cache UI and status line disappear with no signal distinguishing feature-off from empty cache — operators cannot tell misconfiguration from intended behavior.

adjudication.rationale: In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, cache status is derived from `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`, and any credential not present in the returned rows is mapped to `cacheUpdatedAt: null` (`cacheStatusMap.get(...) || null`). The UI (`CredentialActionsDropdown`) then treats `cacheUpdatedAt` truthiness as “has cache” (`const hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt;`), so both “no cache rows exist” and “repository returns []” result in hiding the status/actions. The mock implementation explicitly returns `[]` when calendar-cache is disabled (`CalendarCacheRepositoryMock.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds`), so this design conflates disabled vs empty cache, but the diff doesn’t show how/if the mock is actually wired into the handler (the handler directly `new CalendarCacheRepository()`), making the broader ‘installs where calendar-cache is disabled’ impact not fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] updateManyByCredentialId takes Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput, exposing raw Prisma update semantics at the repository boundary for a call site whose only purpose is a timestamp touch, and the schema reuses the generic SelectedCalendar.updatedAt column (shared with @updatedAt on every other mutation) as the cache-freshness channel. Any other SelectedCalendar update (rename, watch-error set, delegation changes) silently bumps the same updatedAt column, so a future consumer reading it as 'cache last refreshed' gets timestamps polluted by unrelated writes; the next change gets riskier because two meanings share one column with no separate cacheCheckedAt field.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, data: Prisma.SelectedCalendarUpdateInput)` (packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts), which exposes raw Prisma update semantics at the repository boundary, and a call site uses it purely as a “timestamp touch” (`await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` in packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts). That indicates `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` is being repurposed as a signaling mechanism, which is an architectural concern because `updatedAt` is also bumped by any unrelated SelectedCalendar mutation. However, the diff does not show any consumer interpreting `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` as “cache last refreshed” (the UI/cache status added here is based on `CalendarCache.updatedAt`), so the “polluted cache freshness” impact is speculative rather than a concrete defect in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object ({}), which Prisma rejects for updateMany, so the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump the comment promises never happens. Every getAvailability cache-miss path that reaches this line throws a Prisma validation error ("data" must not be empty / no update fields), breaking availability lookups for Google Calendar users whenever cache is cold — and even if tolerated, the empty payload means @updatedAt is not bumped, so the cache-status timestamp the whole PR was built to display is never refreshed by this code path.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the new line `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {});` calls Prisma `updateMany` with an empty `data` object. The repository implementation (`packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts`) forwards this directly to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`, so `data` is `{}` at runtime. Prisma commonly validates `updateMany` and rejects empty updates ("data must not be empty" / no update fields), which would throw on the cache-miss path that reaches this code. Even aside from the throw, an empty update would not reliably achieve the stated goal of bumping `updatedAt`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The PR title and server-side changes implement cache status/delete generically (CalendarCache table, deleteCache mutation, repository method are calendar-type-agnostic), but the UI silently narrows the feature to Google Calendar only via hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt. Users of any other cached calendar provider see no cache status or delete action at all, while their CalendarCache rows keep accumulating — the accepted objective ("calendar cache status and actions") was reduced to a Google-only feature during iteration without an explicit scope decision being recorded; whoever accepted the PR accepted a different surface than what was implemented.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows server-side cache status/delete built without provider checks: `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)` groups by `credentialId` (no integration filter), `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` attaches `cacheUpdatedAt` for every connected calendar, and `deleteCache.handler.ts` deletes `calendarCache` rows by `credentialId` after ownership check. However, the new UI component `CredentialActionsDropdown` explicitly gates cache UI to Google only: `isGoogleCalendar = integrationType === GOOGLE_CALENDAR_TYPE;` and `hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt;`, so non-Google integrations will never see cache status or the delete-cache action even if `cacheUpdatedAt` is provided. This is a concrete scope/product mismatch in the diff, but not provably a correctness defect without knowing intended supported providers for `CalendarCache`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Two parallel mechanisms track "cache last updated" — the new CalendarCache.updatedAt max via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds and the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt bump added in CalendarService.ts — with no single source of truth. The displayed timestamp (CalendarCache._max.updatedAt) and the value GoogleCalendarService writes to refresh cache staleness signals (SelectedCalendar.updatedAt) are different rows updated on different schedules, so the status shown to users will diverge from the mechanism intended to validate it; the next change to cache semantics requires updating both sites or the UI lies. Also note getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns no row for credentials with zero cached entries, which the map lookup silently coerces to null — an empty cache is indistinguishable from "no status".

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly introduces two separate “last updated” signals updated on different paths: (1) UI/connectedCalendars now derives `cacheUpdatedAt` from `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds()` using `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy({ _max: { updatedAt: true }})` and passes it into `CredentialActionsDropdown` for display; (2) `GoogleCalendarService` adds `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` with a comment stating it updates `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt`. These are different tables/rows and there’s nothing in the diff tying them together, so they can diverge and future cache-semantics changes would need coordination across both. Additionally, `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` returns no entry for credentials with zero cache rows; `connectedCalendars.handler.ts` then does `cacheStatusMap.get(...) || null`, making “no cache rows” indistinguishable from “no status/unknown” in the UI. This is an architectural/edge-case concern grounded in the diff, not a proven functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess does not invalidate utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation's onSettled which does. After a user deletes cached data, the dropdown's "Last updated" line continues showing the pre-deletion timestamp if the parent's onSuccess/onChanged doesn't refetch this exact query, presenting a cache status for data that no longer exists.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess?.()`; it does not invalidate/refetch `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike `disconnectMutation` which invalidates in `onSettled`). Since `cacheUpdatedAt` is populated via the `connectedCalendars` query (enriched in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`), deleting cache via `deleteCache.handler.ts` can leave the UI showing a stale “Last updated” value unless the passed `onSuccess/onChanged` callback explicitly refetches/invalidates that query. The diff doesn’t prove what `onChanged` does, so this is a concrete improvement request rather than a definitively verifiable broken behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] A developer-local Tunnelmole test harness with hardcoded paths (/tmp/tmole.log, ../.env, sed -i '' which is macOS-only) is shipped in the production scripts directory as part of a user-facing cache-status feature PR. Linux contributors running the script get a sed syntax error at the GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL rewrite (BSD-only -i '' form), and the repo accumulates an unreproducible dev-only script unrelated to the PR's accepted intent.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new repo script `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` that is clearly a developer-local harness (hardcoded `LOG_FILE="/tmp/tmole.log"`, `ENV_FILE="../.env"`) and uses a macOS/BSD-specific in-place edit form `sed -i '' -E ...` when rewriting `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL`. Including this dev-only, platform-specific script alongside a cache-status feature change is a scope/maintainability concern, and it plausibly breaks for Linux contributors due to the `sed -i ''` form.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US") inside a component that already calls useLocale(), so the accepted i18n intent (all user-facing strings localized, as the new common.json entries show) is broken for this value. Non-English users see a fully translated dropdown except for a US-formatted English date/time, and the i18n pipeline cannot fix it because the locale never flows from t().

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, the cache timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { ... })` even though the component already uses `useLocale()` for translated strings. This hardcodes US formatting for all users, so the dropdown can be localized while the date/time remains US-formatted, and the locale does not flow from `t()` into `Intl.DateTimeFormat`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler throws a bare Error instead of a TRPCError, so an unauthorized or missing credentialId yields an HTTP 500 with an 'Internal Server Error' rather than a 4xx the tRPC contract implies. Users who pass a credentialId they don't own (or a stale one after disconnect) get a 500 error toast; server logs fill with unhandled errors and clients cannot distinguish auth failure from server fault.
matched_golden_ids: Throwing a generic Error for authentication failures results in a 500 response in tRPC. Instead, it should return a structured TRPCError with an appropriate code, such as FORBIDDEN, to accurately reflect the error type.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core issue: throwing a generic/bare Error for auth/authorization failures in a tRPC handler leads to an HTTP 500, and it should instead throw a structured TRPCError with an appropriate 4xx-like code (e.g., FORBIDDEN/UNAUTHORIZED) so clients can distinguish auth failures from server faults.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object `{}`, so it never updates SelectedCalendar.updatedAt despite the comment claiming it does — Prisma updateMany with empty `data` performs no column update (and the new `updatedAt` bump the feature depends on is never written), so the 'Last updated' cache status shown in the dropdown goes stale forever on the webhook/refresh path. After a cache refresh via getAvailability, the CalendarCache rows get new updatedAt values but the SelectedCalendar rows do not (if any consumer reads them), and if Prisma rejects empty data the availability call itself errors; the cache-status UI never reflects the refresh this code was added to record.
matched_golden_ids: The updateManyByCredentialId call uses an empty data object, which prevents Prisma's @updatedAt decorator from updating the updatedAt timestamp. This results in inaccurate cache status tracking, as the timestamp isn't updated when the cache is refreshed. To fix this, explicitly set the updatedAt field.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core issue: updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object, so Prisma performs no update and the @updatedAt timestamp is not bumped, causing stale/inaccurate cache status tracking. This aligns with the golden comment’s suggested fix to explicitly update updatedAt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hard-coded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` even though the component already calls useLocale(), so every non-English user sees an en-US formatted date in an otherwise localized string. Non-English users of the calendar settings page get a jarring English-locale date inside the localized 'cache_last_updated' text; fix is to pass the locale from useLocale() (or use the platform's date formatting util).
matched_golden_ids: Date is formatted with hardcoded 'en-US' locale instead of using the user's locale from useLocale, which can lead to incorrect date representation for users in different locales.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate issue points out that the date is formatted using a hardcoded "en-US" locale via Intl.DateTimeFormat despite the component having access to the user locale from useLocale(), causing incorrect/jarring formatting for non-en-US users. This is the same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The mock's getCacheStatusByCredentialIds returns `[]` (sentinel for 'no cache info') which the handler then maps to `cacheUpdatedAt: null`, making the cache-status UI silently disappear in any environment where calendar-cache is disabled — indistinguishable from a user who genuinely has no cached data. Developers/instances running with the calendar-cache feature disabled cannot exercise or verify the cache-status UI path at all, and any future test relying on the mock verifies the hide-behavior of a sentinel rather than real cache-status semantics.

adjudication.rationale: Diff adds `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` to the calendar-cache repository interface and implements the mock as returning `[]` (calendar-cache disabled) in `calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts`. The connected calendars handler (`connectedCalendars.handler.ts`) then maps missing entries to `cacheUpdatedAt: ... || null`, and the new UI (`CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`) hides cache-status actions when `cacheUpdatedAt` is falsy (`hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt`). So, when the mock is used (disabled cache), the cache-status UI path is unexercisable and indistinguishable from "no cache". This is a diff-grounded testability/semantics concern, not a clear runtime defect shown by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object, which Prisma rejects with a PrismaClientValidationError before any rows are updated. prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: ..., data: {} }) throws "Value argument `data` must not be empty" on every call, so getAvailability/cached-availability-check now throws a 500 on every request for Google credentials instead of bumping updatedAt — the intended updatedAt refresh never happens and the availability endpoint breaks for all Google-connected users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(credentialId, data)` which directly calls `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. In `GoogleCalendarService.checkCacheAndFetchAvailability`, it is invoked as `updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`, i.e., with an empty `data` object. That is at minimum a no-op (so it will not bump `updatedAt` as the comment claims), and Prisma commonly rejects empty `data` on update/updateMany with a validation error. Either way, this change breaks the intended behavior and can cause runtime failures at this call site.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] getCacheStatusByCredentialIds computes the max updatedAt over all rows including expired cache rows, with no filter on expiresAt. Because expired rows are only cleaned lazily (or never, since deleteManyByCredential is a manual action), the Cache Status shown in the dropdown reports a "last updated" timestamp for a credential whose cached entries are all expired, so users see a status that misrepresents the actual cache state.

adjudication.rationale: `CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` uses `prisma.calendarCache.groupBy` with only `where: { credentialId: { in: credentialIds } }` and computes `_max.updatedAt` across *all* rows for that credential, with no filtering on `expiresAt` (which exists on `CalendarCache`). In `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, this `updatedAt` is mapped into `cacheUpdatedAt`, and the UI treats its presence as `hasCache` (`const hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt;`), showing “Cache Status” even if all cache rows are expired. This can therefore present a misleading cache state based on stale/expired rows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation's onSuccess calls onSuccess?.() but never invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars, unlike disconnectMutation which invalidates queries in onSettled. If a caller passes no onSuccess (or the caller's refetch is conditional), the connected-calendars cache retains the pre-delete cacheUpdatedAt, so the dropdown keeps offering 'Delete cached data' and showing a stale timestamp until an unrelated refetch occurs.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown`, `deleteCacheMutation` only calls `onSuccess?.()` and does not invalidate any tRPC queries, whereas `disconnectMutation` explicitly invalidates `utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (and integrations) in `onSettled`. From the diff we can verify the lack of invalidation for the delete-cache path; whether the UI becomes stale depends on what the optional `onSuccess` callback does (not shown in the diff). Adding an invalidate/refetch here would make the new cache-status UI resilient and consistent.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] deleteCache deletes CalendarCache rows but leaves SelectedCalendar.updatedAt untouched, while the code elsewhere treats SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as the sync marker refreshed on cache write. After a user deletes the cache, the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt marker still reflects the last write; any consumer keying off that marker (e.g. webhook-driven invalidation or cache freshness logic) sees a fresh timestamp while the actual cache rows are gone, producing inconsistent state until the next availability fetch backfills it.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows cache writes explicitly “refresh” SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (GoogleCalendarService.fetchAndCacheAvailability calls SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) with the comment “Update SelectedCalendar.updatedAt…”). The new deleteCache handler only deletes prisma.calendarCache rows and does not update SelectedCalendar at all. While the finding’s claim about downstream consumers keying off SelectedCalendar.updatedAt can’t be verified from this diff alone, the diff itself establishes SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as an intended sync marker on cache write, and deleteCache is asymmetrical with that design (potentially leaving a misleading ‘fresh’ updatedAt after cache deletion).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] updateManyByCredentialId is called with an empty data object `{}`, which Prisma rejects with a validation error, so the cache-miss refresh path in getAvailabilityFromCache throws instead of completing. Every cache-miss availability lookup (booking page load, free-busy check) for Google Calendar credentials fails after the fetch and setAvailabilityInCache succeed — the user gets a 500/error instead of availability, and the freshly written cache is never reached as a successful response. Prisma updateMany requires a non-empty `data`; `data: {}` throws `PrismaClientValidationError` at runtime.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` is invoked with an empty `data` object. The repository implementation (`packages/lib/server/repository/selectedCalendar.ts`) passes that directly to `prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany({ where: { credentialId }, data })`. Prisma client validation typically requires `data` to contain at least one updatable field; `data: {}` can raise a `PrismaClientValidationError` at runtime, which would cause this code path to throw after `setAvailabilityInCache` succeeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The handler throws a plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a `TRPCError` with a BAD_REQUEST/FORBIDDEN code, so the client receives an internal-error-shaped 500 rather than the 4xx-shaped error the tRPC mutation contract elsewhere provides. A user clicking delete on a stale credential entry (credential already removed elsewhere) gets an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR-shaped response and the generic 'error_deleting_cache' toast meant for unexpected failures, instead of a proper not-found/bad-request shape; monitoring also records it as a server error rather than client error.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts`, the handler does `throw new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` when the credential lookup fails. In tRPC, throwing a plain `Error` is treated as an `INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR` (500-shaped) rather than a 4xx-shaped `TRPCError` (e.g., `FORBIDDEN`/`NOT_FOUND`/`BAD_REQUEST`). This is a real behavior/contract defect for a user-triggered, expected failure mode (stale/missing credential).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] deleteCache bypasses CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential and calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly, creating a second deletion path that diverges from the repository abstraction (the mock logs and skips, this one does not). Any future behavior added to the repository's deleteManyByCredential (event channel invalidation, cache-bust keys, logging) silently won't apply to the user-facing delete action; operators on calendar-cache-disabled deployments get cache rows deleted here that the mock path would have preserved.

adjudication.rationale: The new TRPC handler `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/deleteCache.handler.ts` deletes via `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })` instead of going through the existing calendar-cache repository abstraction (`ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential`, with a mock that explicitly logs and skips deletion when calendar-cache is disabled). This creates a second, divergent deletion path not covered by the repository layer, so any future behavior centralized in the repository (or mock/disabled behavior) will not apply to this user-facing action.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The handler unconditionally constructs the real CalendarCacheRepository and queries the CalendarCache table even when the calendar-cache feature is disabled (where the rest of the codebase substitutes the Mock repository), so the connected-calendars query always incurs a groupBy on CalendarCache. Every settings-page connected-calendars fetch pays an extra unindexed groupBy on calendarCache (groupBy on credentialId with no composite index covering it beyond the unique key prefix) even on deployments where the cache is disabled, and those rows can be stale legacy data from before the feature flag existed, showing a bogus 'Last updated' to users.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/calendars/connectedCalendars.handler.ts`, the new logic unconditionally imports and instantiates `CalendarCacheRepository` (`new CalendarCacheRepository()`) and always calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds(...)`, adding a DB `groupBy` on `calendarCache` for every connected-calendars request. The diff also shows a `CalendarCacheRepositoryMock` that logs “calendar-cache being disabled”, but this handler does not use any conditional selection/DI to swap in the mock when disabled. That’s a concrete architectural/perf concern introduced by this change, and it can also surface `cacheUpdatedAt` (and thus UI “Cache Status”) whenever rows exist, regardless of any disable mechanism, but the existence/behavior of the feature flag itself isn’t verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] deleteCacheMutation has no onSettled invalidation of `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` (unlike disconnectMutation), so after a successful delete the list still shows the old cache timestamp until onSuccess's parent refetch, and after failure nothing refreshes. When callers pass no `onSuccess` (the prop is optional), a successful cache delete leaves the 'Last updated' row stale in the open dropdown until a manual reload, and any error leaves stale UI with no state reconciliation; only the toast tells the user anything happened.

adjudication.rationale: In `CredentialActionsDropdown.tsx`, `deleteCacheMutation` only shows a toast and calls the optional `onSuccess?.()` callback; it does not invalidate/refetch any TRPC queries (unlike `disconnectMutation`, which invalidates `viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars` and `viewer.apps.integrations` in `onSettled`). From the diff, `cacheUpdatedAt` comes from the `connectedCalendars` query (enriched in `connectedCalendars.handler.ts`), so without an explicit invalidation, the UI will keep showing the previous `cacheUpdatedAt` until some external refetch occurs. The component currently relies on callers to pass an `onSuccess` that triggers a refresh (the wrapper does), which is a fragility/UX consistency issue but not a strictly verifiable broken behavior for the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `sed -i '' -E` uses the macOS-only empty-suffix form; on GNU/Linux sed this fails with "extra characters at the end of h command", so GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated on Linux. Any developer on Linux running the script hits a sed error after the tunnel is already up and the .env write is skipped, leaving a stale webhook URL that makes the subsequent webhook test silently target the old host.

adjudication.rationale: The newly added script `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh` uses `sed -i '' -E ...` to update `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL` in the env file. That `-i ''` (empty backup suffix as a separate argument) is the BSD/macOS sed form and is known to fail on GNU/Linux sed, so on Linux the substitution step can error and the `.env` update won’t occur as intended. This is a cross-platform behavior break introduced by the diff.
